newsitem.title: INDIA: Hundreds arrested, Miss World protest turns violent.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds arrested, Miss World protest turns violent.

text.p: A march against the Miss World beauty pageant erupted in violence in central Bangalore on Saturday and Indian police arrested hundreds of protesters.
A Reuters reporter saw police using batons and tear gas repel a crowd throwing stones and marching on the stadium where the pageant was to be held on Saturday evening.

"It's a police state," Ananth Kumar, a Bangalore-based member of parliament for the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), said as he was bundled into the back of a police van and hit by batons.
Between 500 to 1,000 people were rounded up as police quelled the demonstration, in which several police and protesters were hurt.
The marchers charged the police ranks and began throwing stones. Traffic in the area was blocked for around two hours.
The march was headed for the Chinnaswammy cricket stadium where Miss World is due to be crowned late on Saturday night in front of a global television audience of around two billion.
